subject: Forced to group_by when only mutating

messages.author: d4c7167e7e0c951f
messages.subject: Forced to group_by when only mutating
parts:
dplyr has revolutionized things for me, so thanks a lot for that and your SF Meetup presentation.  I have since switched a lot of production code to it for the obvious performance benefits, and read/usability benefits over other packages.

I seem to crash R a lot with it, and here is an example (using R3.0.2, dplyr 0.1.2): 

I have 2 tbls, A and B, both grouped by the same 2 variables.  
I do an 'outer_join' on them (which is actually an rbind of (left_join(A,B), anti_join(B,A)) after adding missing columns and reordering columns).

This outer_join leaves me a fresh tbl called error_rates, which has no grouped variables.

There are no NAs in this dataset, as I know they have caused problems.
 

Now I want to mutate variables, so I didn't think I need to group_by.  However, if i don't group_by, I get a Segmentation fault: 11

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x8, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .Call("dplyr_mutate_impl", PACKAGE = "dplyr", df, args, env)
 2: mutate_impl(.data, named_dots(...), environment())


Explicitly, this is what causes segfault:

error_rates <- error_rates %.%
    mutate( 
      ntwkRev = sum( rev, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pRev   = round( rev / ntwkRev, 5),
      ntwkImp = sum( imp, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pImp   = round( imp / ntwkImp, 5),
      ntwkError = sum( error, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pError   = round( error / ntwkError, 5),
      activity = error + imp,
      errRate = error / ( imp + error),
      ntwk_errRate = ntwkError / ( ntwkImp + ntwkError),
      #deviation = 1/(1 + exp(-pError)) - .75,
      importance = round( 1000 * (errRate - ntwk_errRate)^3 * errRate * lev_pError, 3)
    )


This produces results as expected:

error_rates <- error_rates %.% group_by( var1_level, var2_level) %.%
    mutate( 
      ntwkRev = sum( rev, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pRev   = round( rev / ntwkRev, 5),
      ntwkImp = sum( imp, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pImp   = round( imp / ntwkImp, 5),
      ntwkError = sum( error, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pError   = round( error / ntwkError, 5),
      activity = error + imp,
      errRate = error / ( imp + error),
      ntwk_errRate = ntwkError / ( ntwkImp + ntwkError),
      #deviation = 1/(1 + exp(-pError)) - .75,
      importance = round( 1000 * (errRate - ntwk_errRate)^3 * errRate * lev_pError, 3)
    )


Note that when I then %.% arrange(desc(importance)) I get another segfault because importance has NaNs.  Perhaps these NaNs produced by the mutate division by 0 are causing the segfault.

Perhaps this is all expected.  Please let me know if it is.  If not, let me know if I can dig deeper to help debug.

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Forced to group_by when only mutating
parts:
I'm really sorry - I've convoluted things.

When I group_by() with mutate() in my example below, it turns out I don't get results as expected.  The result is just that mutate() ends up behaving like summarise() without collapsing the data (so e.g. sum( imp) = imp in every row).  I am testing a variety of things, like splitting up the mutating into separate hierarchical steps.  Nothing is working.  Again there are no NAs or NaNs in the dataset.

So you can understand, I've mining over a variety of grouping variables.  A function of what I am doing works great with 1 grouping variable (and so fast!).  When I try to parameterize the function to mine over 2 grouping_vars, I get this bug.

messages.subject: Re: Forced to group_by when only mutating
parts:
Wow, my problem ended up being from a random part of the code where I reordered columns based on their parameterized names, which lost the Groups in the tbl.  See reproducible example below.  Thanks.


require( dplyr)

grouping_var_1 <- 'C1'
grouping_var_2 <- 'C2'

A <- data.frame( C1 = c( 'a', 'a', 'b', 'b'), C2 = c( 'c', 'c', 'd', 'd'), AN1 = 1:4, AN2 = 5:8)
B <- data.frame( C1 = c( 'A', 'a', 'B', 'b'), C2 = c( 'C', 'c', 'D', 'd'), BN1 = 9:12)

A <- A %.% group_by( C1, C2) %.% summarise( sumA1 = sum(AN1))
B <- B %.% group_by( C1, C2) %.% summarise( sumB1 = sum(BN1))

C <- left_join( A, B)
D <- anti_join( B, A)
D$sumA1 <- 0
D <- D[, names( C)]

E <- rbind( C, D)

G <- E[, c( grouping_var_1, grouping_var_2, 'sumA1', 'sumB1')]

## E and G have different groups

# > E
# Source: local data frame [4 x 4]
# Groups: C1
# 
#   C1 C2 sumA1 sumB1
# 1  a  c     3    10
# 2  b  d     7    12
# 3  B  D     0    11
# 4  A  C     0     9

# > G
# Source: local data frame [4 x 4]
# Groups: 
# 
#   C1 C2 sumA1 sumB1
# 1  a  c     3    10
# 2  b  d     7    12
# 3  B  D     0    11
# 4  A  C     0     9

E %.% mutate( col5 = sum( sumA1)) # works

H <- G %.% regroup( lapply( c( grouping_var_1), as.symbol))
H %.% mutate( col5 = sum( sumA1)) # works

G %.% mutate( col5 = sum( sumA1)) # fails

messages.subject: Re: Forced to group_by when only mutating
parts:
Just to generalize the problem a bit more.  The problem is in re-ordering the tbl in the traditional R way, and not because of using parameter names.  The moral for now is to re-order the columns using dplyr::select().

From the reproducible example below:

require( dplyr)

E <- data.frame( 
  C1       = c( 'a', 'b', 'B', 'A'), 
  C2       = c( 'c', 'd', 'D', 'C'), 
  sumA1 = c( 3, 7, 0, 0), 
  sumB1 = c( 10, 12, 11, 9)
) %.% group_by( C1)


> E

Groups: C1

  C1 C2 sumA1 sumB1
> E[, c('C1','C2','sumA1','sumB1')]; E[, names(E)];  # mutate() will crash with this

Groups:                      

  C1 C2 sumA1 sumB1
> E %.% select( C1, C2, sumA1, sumB1)   # ok on mutate()

Groups: C1

  C1 C2 sumA1 sumB1
